Rewrote the drawing in [Selves.astro](src/components/Selves.astro). What changed:

- **Brush, not lines.** Each stroke is 3–9 bristles offset along the normal, scaled by a pressure curve (lands, holds, lifts) with hand-shake and dry-brush breaks — so strokes taper, split, and carry weight the way a loaded brush does.
- **Constructed head.** Catmull-Rom skull-and-jaw contour with a turn (far side foreshortens), a tilt, and per-sitter proportions — skull, jaw, hair volume, gaze all vary.
- **Hair in three passes** — crown, mass, loose strands — sampled on an ellipse around the skull so it follows the head; below the horizontal the arc stretches, so side locks hang past the ear instead of sticking out.
- **Ink wash** clipped to the face for volume, plus features built properly: lid, crease, lower lid, pupil, brow, nose line and nostril, mouth with lower-lip shade, ear, neck, shoulders, collar. Blossom on the shoulder, tying it to the rest of the page.

One real fix along the way: drawing was gated purely on IntersectionObserver, so anything already on screen at load could sit blank. Now on-screen canvases draw immediately and only off-screen ones wait for their beat.

Verified by rendering the built bundle in headless Chrome, light and dark (above); dark reads the theme tokens at draw time. The browser-pane tab is hidden, which produces no frames — that's why IO and rAF never fire there, not a page bug.

content.text:
Traded the outline-drawing vocabulary for a sumi-e one in [Selves.astro](src/components/Selves.astro):

- **Notan, not outline.** The hair is a wet black mass — a filled shape with a hard edge and a blurred bleed behind it — with loaded 12–30px strokes brushed over it. The face is left as paper.
- **No contour.** Only one fragment of jaw on the shade side plus a chin tick; the lit side of the head has no edge at all and just dissolves into the page.
- **Fewer, weighted marks.** Near eye heavy, far eye faint; a wet smudge for the pupil instead of a bead; one nose line and one loaded nostril tick; one stroke for the mouth. Weight hierarchy does the work drawing detail used to.
- **Form shadow**: a soft crescent hugging the cheek and jaw on the shade side, plus the jaw's shadow on the neck.
- **One accent**: the site's blossom in the lower lip, and a carved seal (knocked out with `destination-out`, so the paper shows through the strokes) placed off-center as the signature.

Dark mode needed real handling — a solid mass of pale ink read as a white slab, so wet passages drop to 22% weight and thin marks get a 1.3× boost when the ink is light. Also guarded `roundRect` for older Safari.

Both renders above come from the built bundle. Same link: **http://localhost:4321/#selves**

Add brushed self-portraits, drawn on canvas at runtime

A new beat between "what i'm bad at" and "rules i keep" holds three
self-portraits, generated in the browser from a fresh seed on every visit
— so the sitter is different each time rather than a baked-in asset.

The drawing is sumi-e rather than line art: the hair is a wet ink mass
(hard-edged fill over a blurred bleed) with loaded strokes over it, the
face is left as paper with only one fragment of jaw, and the features are
a few weighted marks — near eye heavy, far eye faint. The brush itself is
bristles offset along the stroke normal, driven by a pressure curve that
lands, holds and lifts, with dry breaks where it runs out of ink. One
accent of the site's blossom sits in the lower lip, and a carved seal
signs the corner.

Drawing starts when the beat scrolls into view; canvases already on
screen at load draw immediately, so nothing can sit blank if
IntersectionObserver never fires. prefers-reduced-motion paints in one
pass instead of animating. Ink and blossom come from the CSS tokens at
draw time; on dark paper the wet passages drop to 22% weight, since a
solid mass of pale ink reads as a slab rather than as hair.

This is the page's first client-side script, so three claims of "no
javascript" — the meta description, the colophon and the work entry —
are now stated accurately instead.
